issues.title: Coercivity asserted on the full H1 space
issues.failure_explanation: The displayed form controls only the gradient seminorm. For any nonzero constant c, a_{n,θ}(c,c)=0 while ||c||_{H1(D)}>0, contradicting coercivity in the full H1 norm. At most the old form is coercive after imposing Dirichlet data or fixing the constant gauge.
issues.overall_effect: The continuous well-posedness claim is false as stated, and the later compatibility proof cannot infer equality of the two potentials rather than equality only up to a constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix the additive constant by formulating the potential problem on the zero-mean space {q in H^1(D): integral_D q = 0}, equivalently H^1(D)/R, and normalize every time-level potential in that gauge. Poincare's inequality then converts the displayed gradient lower bound into H^1-coercivity. Applying this to φ^{n+θ}−φ^n in the compatibility proof removes the constant kernel, yields equality of the normalized potentials, and leaves the velocity conclusion unchanged.
issues.why_classification: This is not a typo because the proof uses the false coercivity assertion to infer exact equality. Nevertheless, fixing the standard potential gauge and invoking Poincare is a short, routine, local repair that preserves the update and every substantive conclusion in the affected chain.

issues.title: Undefined Gauß-law relaxation coefficient outside its feasible energy range
issues.failure_explanation: An admissible zero-velocity state has E_kin=0, making the old quotient undefined, including the 0/0 case. If E_kin>0 but δE>E_kin, the radicand 1−δE/E_kin is negative. No old hypothesis excludes either case, so the postprocessing construction is not a real-valued, total algorithm on its stated inputs.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed restart postprocessor can be undefined or non-real, and kinetic-energy reduction can restore the previous energy only in the feasible range 0<δE≤E_kin.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the relaxation factor by r = sqrt(1−δE/E_kin) only when 0 < δE <= E_kin, and set r = 1 otherwise, without evaluating the quotient outside that branch. Retain the Gauß-law potential reset on every branch, but state that exact kinetic-energy compensation is guaranteed only in the feasible branch; δE <= 0 already gives no energy increase, whereas δE > E_kin cannot be compensated by scaling the momentum alone.
issues.why_classification: The needed case split is local and requires no new proof architecture, but the issue is not minor: admissible states with zero kinetic energy or with δE > E_kin force withdrawal of the unconditional energy-restoration promise. The resulting total, real-valued Gauß restart remains recognizably the same postprocessor and retains exact compensation wherever algebraically possible, so the weakening is limited rather than major.

issues.title: Undefined operator in the fully discrete velocity update
issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm calls an inverse of B_n even though no operator B_n is defined. The only compatible operator is B_{n,θ}, whose θ-dependent inverse is required by the preceding semidiscrete condensation and by the first equation of the fully discrete system.
issues.overall_effect: The velocity part of the source update is not literally executable, so the well-posedness, energy, and Gauß-law results that use the full update are not established without correcting the operator name.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace every occurrence of the undefined B_n^{-1} in the fully discrete velocity update and its copied downstream proof identities by the already defined B_{n,θ}^{-1}.
issues.why_classification: The preceding semidiscrete condensation, the definition of B_{n,θ}, and the first fully discrete equation uniquely force this correction. The erroneous symbol has no coherent alternative meaning, and correcting it changes no inference, construction, or guarantee in the affected chain.

failure_location.quote:

  result

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it is \emph{not} necessarily true that $\nabla \mathbb H_h

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition needs an h-uniform estimate converting the lumped norms of ∇φ_h and ∇ψ_h into their L2 norms. Assumption ass:regular_mesh only quantifies over V_h^d, but the relevant gradients come from H_h and, on the admitted non-affine meshes, need not belong to V_h^d. The final invocation of that assumption is therefore outside its established scope.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted h-uniform boundedness estimate, and hence the stated fully discrete well-posedness corollary relying on it, are not established for the admitted general non-affine mesh families.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Augment the regular-mesh hypothesis with the h-uniform gradient-lumping stability estimate ||∇q_h||_h <= C_g ||∇q_h||_{L^2(D)^d} for every q_h in H_h. Apply this estimate to both gradient factors in the displayed boundedness calculation; the claimed h-uniform bound and the corresponding well-posedness consequence then follow without changing the scheme.
issues.why_classification: The old proof genuinely invokes its mesh assumption outside that assumption's stated space, so this is not transcriptional. The missing estimate is a standard local finite-element stability qualification for the intended regular mesh sequence; adding it preserves the method, conclusion, scaling, and regular non-affine regime without a new construction or substantial loss.

issues.title: Inadmissible finite-element test substitutions

failure_location.quote: replacing $\vec z_h$ with $\mathcal B_{n,\theta}^\mathsf T\vec z_h$

issues.failure_explanation: The second fully discrete equation is available only for z_h in V_h^d. Multiplication by a variable matrix field or by the discrete density need not preserve that space, so the stated substitutions are not licensed as test functions. Applying I_h to each product restores membership, while the old lumped nodal identities ensure that all subsequent pairings remain unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Without the admissible interpolated tests, the symmetric formulation and the fully discrete energy-balance proof are not formally established, which also interrupts the later energy-inequality and Gauß-residual chain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two product test functions by I_h(B_{n,θ}^T z_h) and I_h(ρ_h^n z_h), respectively. Use the already established nodal identity <I_h f,g>_h = <f,g>_h to recover exactly the same lumped pairings, after which the symmetric formulation, energy balance, and the listed downstream arguments proceed unchanged with respect to this defect.
issues.why_classification: The old proof makes an invalid test-space substitution, so the issue is substantive rather than a typo. Its correction is nevertheless short and local: the required interpolant and nodal identity are already present, no new lemma or proof architecture is needed, and no statement or guarantee in the affected chain is weakened.
